Try it

Bigorna in the browser, without an FM-1. Press Start: the page boots the same package the installer writes (build 69), on an emulated FM-1 — its processor, screen, keys, knobs and audio.

The emulator on a page of its own, with its guide.

Live playback stutters. The emulator can run Bigorna's screen, keys and pages in real time, but not a session playing: six tracks keep both of the FM-1's cores busy, and emulating that takes more than even a fast computer has (an Apple M5 manages under half the speed needed). With the sequencer running, the sound breaks up. To hear the sessions, play the recordings below.

The recordings

Patterns 1 to 9 of session 3, 20 seconds each, recorded in this same emulator, offline: the package above, the three sessions, every sample as the firmware makes it, nothing added afterwards.

Patterns 1 to 7 are the arrangement, built up from pattern 1 to pattern 7. Patterns 8 and 9 are breaks saved as patterns: on the PATTERNS grid, with the 3rd black key held (BREAK), a white key held 0.8 s saves what the break plays — its ratchets, octave leaps, flams, accents and gap — into that pattern slot (see BREAK).

The sessions in the emulator

The emulator starts with the same three sessions, and opens on session 3 at pattern 7.

  1. Press Start, then PLAY (Space) to start pattern 7 (it stutters, as above).
  2. Press ARP (9) for the PATTERNS grid. Patterns 1 to 9 hold steps; the one playing is outlined.
  3. Load another pattern: click its white key (pattern 1 is the first white key on the left, pattern 9 the ninth), or choose it with PRESETS (↓ ↑) and press ARP. While the sequencer plays, the new pattern starts at the end of the chosen track's steps.
  4. Go through patterns 1 to 7 in order to see how the arrangement is built: each pattern's steps (STEP, O), and the tracks' state it brings back (mutes, machine, octave, level, pan). Patterns 8 and 9 hold the two breaks.

On the computer's keyboard, A S D F G are the 5th to 9th white keys: on the grid, patterns 5 to 9.

Playing it

Click or drag the panel as you would press and turn the FM-1's: drag a knob up or down, or scroll over it. A key held with the mouse stays held while you press another on the computer's keyboard — hold SHIFT (the last black key) with the mouse, then press 7 for SHIFT + HOME. The panel carries the FM-1's own labels; under Bigorna the six top buttons are tracks 1 to 6 (see The panel).

What to know

  • The emulator starts at the FM-1's own clock, 240 MHz. A lower clock (below the panel) is lighter, but not enough for a session to play smoothly, and Bigorna then has fewer cycles than on an FM-1.
  • Sessions saved with SAVE stay in this browser, for this build only; a new build starts again with the three sessions. The emulator's full page can export them to a file.
  • MIDI in works in Chrome, Edge and Firefox (choose the input below the panel). There is no MIDI out, no USB and no installing from here: to put Bigorna on an FM-1, see Install.
  • It is an emulation: timing, load and sound are close to the FM-1's, not the same.

The emulator

The emulator is fm1-emu, by Joakim Eriksson (MIT licence), copied here with a catalog that holds only Bigorna and one change: with nothing saved in the browser, it starts with the three sessions. It is not made by M-VAVE, and Bigorna's author did not write it.

Developed by Nuno Zimas. Firmware: GPL-3.0. Website and logo: MIT. Source on GitHub.
